concerns.text: T101 instructs loading `code/contracts/raw_halo.schema.yaml`, but no such contract exists — plan.md's project structure and data-model.md list only `halo.schema.yaml` and `results.schema.yaml`. The task's verification ('running python -m code.data.preprocess completes... validates...') will fail on a missing schema file. Point it at `code/contracts/halo.schema.yaml` (or define the new contract).

T104's verification demands '≥9 KS records (3 metrics × mass bins)', but FR-008 defines KS tests between low vs. high ENVIRONMENT bins, and results.schema.yaml's `bin_comparison` enum permits only `low_vs_high`/`mass_correlation`. As written the task cannot both satisfy its own count check and produce schema-valid records. Specify the actual test matrix (e.g., 3 metrics × 2 mass bins × low_vs_high = 6, or 3 metrics × 3 environment splits) consistent with the schema.

T105 requires appending a `bullock_comparison` record (RMSE, mean difference, per-bin residuals) to `results/statistics.json`, but results.schema.yaml has `additionalProperties: false` and no Bullock fields/enums. The mandated artifact would fail the schema validation T104 simultaneously enforces. Either write the Bullock block to a separate file (e.g. `results/bullock_comparison.json`) or amend the contract first.

Header claims 'Previously verified tasks are preserved as checked', yet every listed task T003–T030 is an unchecked `- [ ]` box while only T031–T037 are `[X]`. An implementer cannot determine which prior tasks are actually done; mark verified items `[X]` or state explicitly that unchecked items still require execution.

T108's verification 'assert duration < 21600 s on the free-tier CPU runner' is not verifiable from the task itself — the assert runs inside the script, but the verification clause should state where the measured duration is checked (e.g. timing.json `duration_s < 21600`) and that the assert must not be a no-op on non-CI machines.

T107 covers three edge cases but omits the spec's 'catalog missing a required column → halt with explicit error' edge case; a fourth test (e.g. `test_missing_velocity_column_halts`) would make the edge-case task fully self-contained against spec.md's Edge Cases list.
